answer.why: The application says the business is wholly owned by someone who is not on the register: Companies House lists the director as the only person with significant control. Undeclared or misdeclared ownership is a standard reason to stop an application. This issue was planted into a real, ordinary company's application, so the label is correct by construction. Decline.

default companies house registered office address applied

answer.why: An 11-month-old company registered for crypto and investment activity, with no FCA registration, one director who is also the only owner, no website, and no search results. The registrar had moved its registered office, and the director's service address, to the Companies House default address because they were not valid. Three months after the case date the Insolvency Service had it wound up in the public interest. Decline.
